subject: Rivertide pilot economics — commitment path and next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@rivertide.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Rivertide pilot economics & commitment pathway

Liam — thanks again for the 30-min sync today. Couple quick notes to lock in what we heard and proposed next steps. If anything below reads differently than you remember, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Token spend variability: nightly batch jobs + user chat spikes cause unpredictable monthly bills.
- Latency spikes at peak putting some flows (fraud scoring, user-facing chat) over 300ms p95.
- Procurement + security constraint: SOC2 evidence + clear unit economics required before any commitment.
- Tight pilot budget in Q2: you mentioned a ~$150k cap unless we show clear upside.

Primary goals (success criteria for pilot)
- Reduce per-interaction unit cost by ~50–65% via serving levers while preserving quality.
- Maintain p95 generation latency <= 250ms for core inference flows.
- Deliver a 6-week pilot that yields a reproducible savings model for scale.

Our recommended pilot scope (minimal viable to prove ROI)
- Duration: 6 weeks (2 weeks config/sim + 4 weeks live sample traffic).
- Target load: start with ~100k tokens/day (scale to 350k tokens/day burst).
- Config: hosted Dedicated pool with 1 dedicated GPU cluster, continuous batching enabled, prefix/KV caching for stable prompts, and a 4-bit quantized model variant for non-critical scoring.

Top levers we’ll test and expected impact (prelim)
- Continuous batching (latency-aware): 25–40% token cost reduction for steady-state traffic.
- Prefix/KV caching (fraud scoring templates): up to 50% token/time savings on repetitive requests.
- Quantized model path (4-bit): 20–35% cost reduction for background scoring where tolerance for slight quality delta is acceptable.
- Routing to lower-cost region during non-peak windows: additional 8–12% savings.

Preliminary ROI snapshot (very conservative)
- Baseline estimate: $0.030 per 1k tokens (hosted mixed model).
- Expected blended post-optimization: ~$0.011–0.015 per 1k tokens.
- If we achieve the 50%+ reduction on your steady-state, the pilot budget (at 150k cap) shows a 3–5x modeled savings within 6 months of ramp. I put a line-itemized model in the attached Rivertide-prelim-econ.xlsx.

Immediate next steps (what we need from you)
1) Procurement: SOC2 report + specific procurement contacts (procurement@rivertide.com ok).
2) Data sample: 48–72h anonymized traffic sample (for real batching sims) — upload link in related_links.
3) Decision: confirm whether you can stretch to $200k if we can demonstrate >55% unit-cost reduction in the simulation.

What we’ll deliver in the next 7 business days
- SOW + draft pricing tied to the pilot milestones (attached redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf).
- A short simulation run on your 48h sample and a savings projection within 72 hours of receipt.

Proposed calendar: quick procurement intro + technical kickoff next Thursday morning (your time). I’ll put a tentative slot on the thread.

Thanks again — excited to get you a repeatable cost path.

— Michael Grant
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Rivertide-prelim-econ.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (SOW draft)

From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@rivertide.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@rivertide.com
Date: 2027-03-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Rivertide pilot economics & commitment pathway

Michael — thanks for the crisp recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Budget: the $150k pilot cap is what procurement will sign off on today. We can stretch to $200k only if your simulation shows >55% sustainable unit-cost improvement and an execution path to meet our p95 latency targets.
2) Timeline: procurement needs all security docs (SOC2, encryption details, data retention policy) before the end of the month. If you can provide SOC2 and the SOW this week, we can expedite.
3) On-prem: if the simulation indicates we cannot hit latency/SLOs in hosted mode, procurement will require an on-prem or VPC option. Please include that as a fallback in the SOW.
4) Requested deliverable: a simple one-line unit cost table for 1M requests (avg tokens per request = 120) — baseline vs pilot optimized. That’s what the execs will want to see.

I’ll loop in procurement separately (they’re cc’d). We’re good to run the 48h sample but need instructions for anonymization and upload.

— Liam Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Rivertide Labs
liam.chen@rivertide.com

- SOW: I’ve attached the pilot SOW draft (redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf) to this email and to the drive link in related_links. It includes an explicit on-prem fallback section and milestone-based payments tied to simulation and latency gating.

See you Thursday — we’ll come prepared with a targeted set of experiments and concrete trade-offs.
